text:
devon: ALERT: ALB removed ~18 targets across edge-alloc us-west-2 in last 10m, pods went NotReady. Rolling flaps observed on a couple of services. Anyone seeing recent deregisters?

infra-bot: monitoring: ALB target health -> unhealthy (HTTP/connection) for target group tg-edge-prod-1; 18 targets deregistered over 00:09:42.

maya: Is this a readiness probe issue? App logs show /ready returned 200 consistently on the impacted pods.

sam: I tried curling the pod from the node and got 200. From the ALB perspective we're seeing timeouts and occasional 502/connection resets. Example I ran:
```
curl -svS http://10.0.45.82:8080/ready
> 200 OK
```

devon: Pulled a tcpdump on the pod interface. ALB SYN arrives, pod SYN-ACK goes out, then ALB sends RST. Looks like the ALB healthcheck connection state gets confused mid-handshake — possibly due to source port churn on our SNAT path.

ops-sre: We've hit similar behavior when ephemeral port pool got exhausted and ports were recycled while external healthchecker still had state for previous flows. Could be ephemeral port exhaustion on the nodes doing SNAT.

sam: Checked node values: /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range -> "32768 60999" (default). Healthchecks are short-lived TCP connects at a fairly high rate, so reuse is plausible.

devon: Proposed action: 1) bump ip_local_port_range to "10240 65535" on edge nodes 2) for a workaround consider moving ALB healthchecks to nodePort so they hit node IPs (bypass SNAT) or use an NLB with stable source IPs/target-type=ip.

maya: NodePort would avoid SNAT for probes, proxy-protocol could also help but requires app changes. Which is less risky for a canary?

ops-sre: Proxy-protocol needs app support so that's heavier. I'll roll the sysctl change to a single ASG to test, and then flip a service probe to nodePort in a canary namespace.

deploy-bot: ops:sysctl-change executed on edge-asg-a (rolling), set net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range=10240 65535 on batch of nodes.

sam: After the sysctl bump, failure rate dropped ~60% in the canary cluster. ALB still removed 2 targets in the last 5m though. Looks like port range helped but didn't fully eliminate flaps.

devon: Next steps: full roll of the ephemeral-port bump across edge ASGs and migrate sensitive healthchecks to nodePort for the next deploy window. Owner: ops-sre. If flaps persist after the roll, we'll trial an NLB target-ip approach and revisit connection tracking tuning. Follow-up in #incidents if we see more deregisters.
